issues.legal_issue: An Additional District Magistrate vested with the powers of a District Magistrate under the general criminal procedure law is not thereby authorized to exercise a power delegated specifically to District Magistrates.
material_facts: The Central Government delegated its power to requisition immovable property to specified authorities, including District Magistrates.

The requisitioning order was made by an Additional District Magistrate who had been vested with all the powers of a District Magistrate under the general criminal procedure law, but had not been appointed as the District Magistrate.
The order requisitioned a shop occupied by a tenant.
issues.conclusion: The Additional District Magistrate was not empowered to make the requisitioning order under the delegation. The appeal was allowed and the order was quashed.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 29 and 40(1) of the Defence of India Act, 1962, a delegation of the Central Government’s requisitioning power to District Magistrates does not extend to an Additional District Magistrate merely because the latter is vested with a District Magistrate’s powers under section 10(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The notification’s words are to be read as written unless context requires otherwise; an Additional District Magistrate and a District Magistrate are distinct authorities. Given the drastic character of requisitioning and its effect on property rights protected by Article 19(1)(f), the delegation is understood as selecting an officer of the District Magistrate’s status. The Court approved and applied Prabhulal Ramlal Kabra v. Emperor, A.I.R. 1944 Nag. 84. It distinguished Ajaib Singh v. State of Punjab, [1965] 2 S.C.R. 845, because the relevant delegation provisions there expressly imposed a minimum-rank requirement, and Central Talkies Ltd. v. Dwarka Prasad, [1961] 3 S.C.R. 495, because the statute there authorized the District Magistrate to assign functions to another officer.

predicates.requisition_delegation_case: The proceeding challenges an order made under a delegated power to requisition immovable property.
predicates.power_delegated_specifically_to_district: The delegation identifies District Magistrates as authorized to exercise the power.
predicates.actor_is_additional_magistrate: The official who made the order held the office of Additional District Magistrate rather than District Magistrate.
predicates.actor_only_vested_with_district_magistra: The official had been given the powers of a District Magistrate under general law but had not been appointed to that office.

issues.definition: When a requisition-delegation proceeding involves a power delegated specifically to District Magistrates and an order made by an Additional District Magistrate vested only with a District Magistrate’s powers, the Additional District Magistrate lacks authority under that delegation.
